nodes.name: Normalize Lead Payload
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Normalize incoming lead records to a stable schema Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Score the Lead
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Score each lead 0-100 from simple heuristics Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Assign Round-Robin Owner
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Round-robin owner assignment Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Route by Heat
nodes.notes: Routes each item to one of 3 lanes: hot, warm + fallback. Watch out: Unmatched items go to the fallback output; without one they are silently dropped.

nodes.name: Hot → HubSpot + Instant Ping
nodes.notes: Creates or updates a HubSpot contact by email — HubSpot is the CRM system of record for this pipeline. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: HubSpot private-app token. HubSpot → Settings → Integrations → Private Apps → create app → copy the token.

nodes.name: Notify Assigned Owner
nodes.notes: Posts a message to Slack — a low-latency way for the team to see automation activity without checking a dashboard. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Slack OAuth2. Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.

nodes.name: Warm → Drip via Outlook
nodes.notes: Sends an email via Microsoft Outlook — recipient comes from the item's email field. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Microsoft OAuth2. Azure Portal → App registrations → Microsoft Graph → Mail.Send / Mail.Read.

nodes.name: Cold → Park in Nurture List
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'tracking sheet' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Combine Lead Paths
nodes.notes: Rejoins 3 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: Stamp Completion Time
nodes.notes: Stamps completedAt with the current time for auditing.

nodes.name: Persist Run Metadata
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Fingerprint for Idempotency
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Build a stable idempotency key per lead (djb2 hash, no deps) Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Drop Already-Processed Items
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

nodes.name: Serialize Run Output (CSV)
nodes.notes: Serializes items to a CSV binary file.

nodes.name: Archive Row Snapshot

# Capture demo requests for outreach

**Pattern:** Lead Capture & Routing · **Level:** Advanced · **Trigger:** Form

## Overview

Starts when the form is submitted, and covers outreach work end to end across Google Sheets, Outlook, Slack and HubSpot.

It moves through 19 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. New Lead Form Submission
2. Normalize Lead Payload
3. Score the Lead
4. Assign Round-Robin Owner
5. Route by Heat
6. Hot → HubSpot + Instant Ping
7. Notify Assigned Owner
8. Warm → Drip via Outlook
9. Cold → Park in Nurture List
10. Combine Lead Paths
11. Stamp Completion Time
12. Persist Run Metadata
13. Fingerprint for Idempotency
14. Drop Already-Processed Items
15. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
16. Archive Row Snapshot
17. Summarize Run Stats
18. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
19. Send Summary to Outlook

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Outlook → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing outreach work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

New Lead Form Submission → Normalize Lead Payload → Score the Lead → Assign Round-Robin Owner → Route by Heat → Hot → HubSpot + Instant Ping → Notify Assigned Owner → Warm → Drip via Outlook → Cold → Park in Nurture List → Combine Lead Paths → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Row Snapshot → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Outlook → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Outlook → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Google Sheets and Outlook aligned by hand for outreach
- Intake checked for completeness before it is stored in Google Sheets, for outreach
- Outreach work where "Normalize Lead Payload" is still a manual step before Google Sheets
- Outreach work that only reaches Google Sheets when a form is submitted, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Google Sheets and Outlook in step for outreach, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Google Sheets or Outlook are skipped, across all 22 nodes of this outreach build
- A failed Google Sheets or Outlook call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 22 nodes in this outreach build
- Branches rejoin before Google Sheets, so a outreach run reports once rather than 22 times
- Every outreach run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Google Sheets

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Google OAuth2 / service account; HubSpot private-app token; Microsoft OAuth2; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Round-robin owner assignment happens right after scoring, before routing — every lead gets an accountable owner regardless of tier, so even a 'cold' lead parked in the nurture list is someone's responsibility later, not an anonymous row in a spreadsheet.

## Practice exercises

Already production-grade — deepen your understanding:

1. Change the hot/warm threshold values and watch the tier distribution shift.
2. Add a 4th owner to the round-robin pool.
3. Add a follow-up wait+check to the warm-drip branch, similar to the drip-ladder spine.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**HubSpot private-app token**
HubSpot → Settings → Integrations → Private Apps → create app → copy the token.
_Gotcha:_ Grant the CRM scopes you need; legacy API keys are deprecated and will not work.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

**Microsoft OAuth2**
Azure Portal → App registrations → Microsoft Graph → Mail.Send / Mail.Read.
_Gotcha:_ Choose delegated vs application permissions deliberately; they behave differently.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your outreach process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Outlook: use `Mail.Send` alone if nothing here reads the mailbox.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- HubSpot: a private-app token carrying only the CRM scopes these nodes use — legacy API keys are deprecated and over-broad.

**Do not log**
outreach payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
